'''Giovanni Frattini''' (8 January 1852 – 21 July 1925) was an Italian [[mathematician]], noted for his contributions to [[group theory]].

==Biography==
Frattini entered the [[Sapienza University of Rome|University of Rome]] in 1869, where he studied [[mathematics]] with [[Giuseppe Battaglini]], [[Eugenio Beltrami]], and [[Luigi Cremona]], obtaining his [[Laurea]] in 1875.

In 1885 he published a paper where he defined a certain [[subgroup]] of a [[finite group]].  This subgroup, now known as the [[Frattini subgroup]], is the subgroup <math>\Phi(G)</math> generated by all the non-generators of the group <math>G</math>. He showed that <math>\Phi(G)</math> is [[Nilpotent group|nilpotent]] and, in so doing, developed a method of proof known today as [[Frattini's argument]].<ref>{{cite journal|first=Giovanni|last= Frattini|title=Intorno alla generazione dei gruppi di operazioni (english translation)|journal=Accademia dei Lincei, Rendiconti |series=(4)|volume= I|pages=281–285, 455–457|year= 1885| jfm=17.0097.01| url=http://www.advgrouptheory.com/GTArchivum/Frattini/FrattiniPaper1885Transl.pdf}} (original paper available at [http://emeroteca.braidense.it/beic_attacc/sfoglia_articolo.php?IDTestata=927&CodScheda=00AI&IDT=34&IDV=293&IDF=0&IDA=18340 Emeroteca Braidense])</ref>

Besides group theory, he also studied
differential geometry and the analysis of second degree indeterminates.
<ref>Emaldi, Maurizio,
Giovanni Frattini 1852–1925,
Irish Math. Soc. Bull. No. 23 (1989), 57–61.</ref>
